Do You Feel Like We Do
Peter Frampton with Louis Cato & the Late Show Band
Commented on #69 📝 move written content into .yaml files

Related: #24 The current docs have their source in one branch and then the CI merges the updates into version-specific docs which are what are published: We could replicate that here, either keeping the source and published pages in separate branches or in separate directories.
Alternatively have one more level of depth like . └── assets (3 more lines were trimmed) or . ├── nightly (or `develop`) (5 more lines were trimmed) and have the CI make a copy from nightly into a release branch when we cut a new release, but depending on which aspects of the site will be constant across versions vs which will be changing, these kinds of hybrid structures could get complicated.

div.div: Pytests: getting error function uses no argument error
singularity run error: No valid /bin/sh in container
For me this suggestion did the trick: when changing Singularity versions, configuration, or installation path, run make clean between make and make install in the installation process.
